We're finalizing our GL mapping and need confirmation on VAT treatment for a few subscriptions.

Hi Anna,

Thanks — quick answer up front: the VAT treatment depends on how the commercial flow is structured (customer of record vs reseller relationship), and whether you are reselling Redwood's service or acting as a reseller taking title to the service. Short version:

- If Heliosoft is the contracting customer of record (we invoice Heliosoft directly) and Heliosoft is in the EU, we generally issue a net invoice and you self-account via reverse-charge for EU B2B services (place-of-supply = Germany). You provide a valid DE VAT ID and we record that.

- For APAC end-customer usage billed under the same Heliosoft contract but supplied through a Singapore reseller, local GST in Singapore may apply where the place-of-supply is deemed to be Singapore (e.g., if ResellCo is the supplier of record to end customers). In practice there are two common patterns:
  1) Reseller as supplier of record: ResellCo invoices the end customer and is responsible for local GST. Redwood invoices Heliosoft (reseller partner) or ResellCo depending on the partner agreement.
  2) Supplier of record Heliosoft: If Heliosoft resells under your agreement but Heliosoft is clearly the supplier to the end-customer, then Heliosoft handles local GST and Redwood may still invoice Heliosoft net (reverse-charge for EU B2B) — but you'd need to ensure local GST obligations are met.

We need to confirm which party is the supplier of record for the APAC transactions and whether Redwood will be recognized on local tax returns.

I'll loop in Neha (tax) and Marissa (billing ops) to suggest the cleanest invoice flow and any splits required.

Regards,

Hi all,

Couple of practical next steps from tax/compliance perspective:

1) Please confirm contract counterparties and which entity appears on the customer's invoice (Heliosoft vs ResellCo). If Heliosoft remains customer of record and we invoice Heliosoft in DE, we will require the DE VAT ID (provided) and will mark the invoice as B2B intra-EU supply (reverse-charge).

2) If APAC end-customer usage needs to be taxed locally, the simplest operational approach is to split billing by region: Redwood can generate region-tagged invoice lines (EU vs APAC) and apply no VAT on the EU lines when reverse-charge applies; APAC lines would be taxable if supplied by Redwood into APAC jurisdiction. That requires Heliosoft/reseller to accept split invoices and may need changes to your billing system.

3) Alternatively, ResellCo can become the billed party for APAC transactions. In that case they would register for GST and handle local remittance; Redwood would invoice ResellCo Singapore with appropriate tax treatment (local GST where applicable).

Attaching a short checklist for evidence we need to record tax treatment (VAT cert, reseller agreement, flow diagram). Marissa — can ops share a draft split-invoice PDF so the customer sees how lines would appear?
